text: That's an unusual starting point; to guide our investigation, do you notice any stiffness or reduced range of motion in your left shoulder, particularly when reaching behind your back or overhead?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age and diabetes, would you describe the pain as a deep ache in the joint itself, or more like surface tenderness near the front of the shoulder? Also, does applying ice or heat provide any relief?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Adhesive Capsulitis (Frozen Shoulder) secondary to Diabetes Mellitus.
